text: Python is a high-level, dynamically typed programming language widely used for data science, scripting, and web development.
FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) is a library for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors, supporting both exact and approximate nearest-neighbor search.
BM25 is a bag-of-words ranking function used by search engines to estimate the relevance of documents to a given search query, based on term frequency and inverse document frequency.
Sentence-transformers like all-MiniLM-L6-v2 produce dense vector embeddings of sentences that capture semantic meaning, enabling similarity comparisons via cosine distance.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combines a retriever that fetches relevant documents with a language model that generates answers grounded in that retrieved context.
Vector databases such as Pinecone, Weaviate, and Milvus store embeddings and support approximate nearest-neighbor search at scale for semantic retrieval applications.
Recall and precision are core information retrieval metrics: recall measures the fraction of relevant items retrieved, while precision measures the fraction of retrieved items that are relevant.
Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) is the average of the reciprocal of the rank of the first relevant result across a set of queries, rewarding systems that place relevant results near the top.
